FACT-5.gloss: The WHO recommends a broad-spectrum sunscreen with an SPF of at least 15
FACT-5.verify_reason: UNVERIFIED: The only source found was an FDA label that recommends a broad-spectrum SPF of 15 or higher. It doesn't name the WHO.

FACT-6.gloss: An SPF of 5 would likely give insufficient protection against UVA and UVB
FACT-6.verify_reason: UNVERIFIED: I found no source on how well SPF 5 protects against UVA and UVB.

FACT-7.gloss: An SPF of 10 falls short of the WHO recommendation of at least 15
FACT-7.verify_reason: UNVERIFIED: The FDA label gives an SPF 15 minimum, but I found no WHO source to compare SPF 10 against.

FACT-8.gloss: An SPF of 15 meets the basic WHO requirement and is considered adequate protection

RULE-1.gloss: An option whose SPF is insufficient is not the answer

RULE-2.gloss: An option whose SPF is adequate and equals the WHO-recommended minimum is the answer

INF-1.gloss: Option A is not the answer, from FACT-1, FACT-6, and RULE-1 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-2.gloss: Option B is not the answer, from FACT-2, FACT-7, and RULE-1 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens

INF-3.gloss: Option C is the answer, from FACT-3, FACT-8, FACT-5, and RULE-2 by Universal Instantiation and Modus Ponens
